title: Test Automation
sources: Python Automation Engineer Handbook (complete edition, Oct 2026)
Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Automation Handbook (Edition 1.0, Oct 2026)

challenges.title: What a fixture is
challenges.description: pytest fixtures replace most setUp/tearDown code in automation frameworks.
challenges.instructions: Which description of a pytest fixture is correct?
hints: Tests receive fixtures as arguments.
Code after yield in a fixture runs as teardown.
challenges.source: Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Ch. 25 pytest; API & Protocol Automation Handbook Q27
options: A function that provides set-up (and optional teardown) to tests that request it by parameter name
A plugin that generates HTML reports
A configuration file that lists tests to skip
A decorator that makes a test run twice

challenges.title: Counting parametrised cases
challenges.description: Two parametrize decorators are stacked on one test.
challenges.instructions: How many test cases does pytest collect from this function? Type a number.
hints: Stacked parametrize decorators combine as a cross product.
2 firmware versions × 3 interfaces.
challenges.explanation:
Stacking parametrize decorators generates every combination: 2 × 3 = 6 test cases, each reported with its
            own ID such as test_sel_clear[lan-2.13].
challenges.source: Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Ch. 25 pytest (parametrize)

challenges.title: Fixture teardown
challenges.description: This fixture must close the BMC session after each test, even when the test fails.
challenges.instructions: Fill the blank so the test receives the session and the close runs afterwards.
hints: return would end the fixture before teardown.
The keyword pauses the function and resumes it later.
challenges.explanation:
yield hands the session to the test and pauses the fixture. After the test finishes, pass or fail, pytest
         resumes the fixture and the code after yield runs as teardown.
challenges.source: Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Ch. 25 pytest (fixtures)

challenges.title: conftest.py
challenges.description: Several test modules need the same bmc_session fixture.
challenges.instructions: Where should the shared fixture live?
hints: No import is needed for fixtures in this file.
Its fixtures apply to its directory and below.
challenges.explanation:
pytest automatically loads conftest.py files and makes their fixtures and hooks available to tests in that
       directory and its subdirectories, without imports.
challenges.source: Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Ch. 25 pytest; API & Protocol Automation Handbook Q28
options: In pytest's site-packages folder
In a conftest.py in the tests directory; pytest discovers it automatically
In setup.py
In every test file, copied

challenges.title: Comparing measured values
challenges.description: A test asserts that a measured PSU efficiency equals the expected 0.94.
challenges.instructions: Which assertion is the right one?
hints: Floating-point values are rarely exactly equal.
pytest has a helper for tolerant comparisons.
challenges.explanation:
pytest.approx compares within a tolerance, which is what measurements need. Exact float equality fails for
       tiny representation errors, string comparison is fragile, and is compares identity.
challenges.source: Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Ch. 25 pytest; API & Protocol Automation Handbook Q33
options: assert efficiency == 0.94
assert efficiency is 0.94
assert efficiency == pytest.approx(0.94, abs=0.005)
assert str(efficiency) == "0.94"

challenges.title: The assertion that never fails
challenges.description: A status test has never failed, even against a BMC returning 500.
hints: What type is (a, b)?
Is a non-empty tuple truthy?
challenges.explanation:
assert (x, "msg") asserts a two-item tuple, which is always true. Write assert resp.status_code == 200,
        "service root unavailable" without the parentheses. Python even emits a SyntaxWarning for this.
challenges.source: Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Ch. 25 pytest; Ch. 37 Code Quality
options: client.get must be awaited
The parentheses build a non-empty tuple, which is always truthy, so the assert always passes
The message must come before the condition
assert cannot compare integers

challenges.title: Expecting an exception
challenges.description: A parser must reject a malformed SEL entry with ValueError.
challenges.instructions: Fill the blank to assert that the exception is raised.
hints: It is used as a context manager.
The test fails if no exception occurs.
challenges.explanation:
pytest.raises(ValueError) passes if the block raises ValueError (or a subclass) and fails if it does not.
         Add match="..." to check the message too.
challenges.source: Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Ch. 25 pytest
challenges.code:
import pytest

def test_rejects_bad_entry():
    with pytest.____(ValueError):
        parse_sel_entry("garbage")

challenges.title: Session fixtures and xdist
challenges.description: You start running the suite with pytest -n 4 (pytest-xdist). A session-scoped fixture that powers on the DUT now misbehaves.
hints: How many processes does -n 4 start?
Fixture scope is per process.
challenges.explanation:
xdist starts separate worker processes and each one has its own test session, so a session fixture runs in
       every worker. Shared hardware needs a lock (for example a file lock) or one device per worker.
challenges.source: API & Protocol Automation Handbook Q35; Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Ch. 25
options: Session fixtures run only after all tests
xdist disables fixtures
xdist runs tests in a random Python version
Each xdist worker is a separate process with its own session, so the fixture runs once per worker

challenges.title: Module-scoped setup
challenges.description: Three tests in one module use the same module-scoped fixture.
challenges.instructions: How many times is "download image" printed when this module runs? Type a number.
hints: scope="module" creates the fixture once per module.
All three tests share the cached value.
challenges.explanation:
A module-scoped fixture is created the first time a test in the module needs it and reused for the
            rest of the module, so the download runs once.
challenges.source: Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Ch. 25 pytest (fixture scope)
challenges.code:
import pytest

@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def firmware_image():
    print("download image")
    return "bmc-2.14.1.bin"

def test_size(firmware_image): ...
def test_signature(firmware_image): ...
def test_version(firmware_image): ...

challenges.title: Faking the environment
challenges.description: A function reads the BMC address from the BMC_HOST environment variable.
challenges.instructions: What is the cleanest way to test it?
hints: pytest has a built-in fixture for temporary changes.
Changes should be undone after the test.
challenges.explanation:
monkeypatch.setenv sets the variable for one test and restores the original value automatically, so tests
       stay isolated.
challenges.source: API & Protocol Automation Handbook Q31; Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Ch. 26 unittest and Mocking
options: Use the monkeypatch fixture: monkeypatch.setenv("BMC_HOST", "10.0.0.5")
Edit the real environment of the CI agent
Hard-code the address in the function
Skip the test

challenges.title: Inside a pytest run
challenges.description: Order what pytest does when you run a suite.
challenges.instructions: Put the phases in the order pytest performs them for a test that uses a fixture.
hints: Nothing can run before pytest knows what exists.
Teardown follows the test.
challenges.explanation:
pytest first collects tests, then for each test sets up fixtures, runs the test and tears the fixtures
            down. Reports such as --junitxml are written at the end of the session.
challenges.source: Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Ch. 25 pytest; Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 15 Pytest Reports
steps: Write the results report (for example JUnit XML)

challenges.title: Order-dependent tests
challenges.description: test_count passes only when test_add runs first.
hints: Could test_count pass if run alone?
Each test should create its own data.
challenges.explanation:
Tests must be independent. test_count relies on state created by test_add, so running it alone, in a
        different order or in parallel fails. Create the data in a fixture so each test gets a fresh list.
challenges.source: Python Automation Engineer Handbook · Ch. 37 Code Quality and Testing Standards
options: Tests share a module-level list, so one test depends on another's side effects
append() returns None
len() does not work on lists
Test names must start with check_

challenges.title: Selecting by marker
hints: -m takes a boolean expression over markers.
not inverts the selection.
challenges.explanation:
-m selects tests by marker expression; not hardware deselects marked tests. This lets CI run the
       simulator-only subset on every commit and the hardware subset on a lab agent.
challenges.source: Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 17 Test Selection and Regression Strategies
options: Fails if any hardware test exists
Runs every test except those marked hardware
Deletes the hardware marker
Runs only the hardware tests

challenges.title: JUnit XML for Jenkins
challenges.description: Jenkins needs a JUnit XML report to show test trends.
challenges.instructions: Write the pytest command that runs the tests and writes a JUnit XML report to reports/junit.xml.
hints: The option name contains junit and xml.
It takes the output path after an = sign.
challenges.explanation:
--junitxml=PATH (also spelled --junit-xml) writes a JUnit-format report that Jenkins' junit step can
           publish. python -m pytest is equivalent and ensures the right interpreter's pytest is used.
challenges.source: Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 15 Pytest Reports and Test Results

challenges.title: Handling a flaky test
challenges.description: A Redfish test fails about once in twenty nightly runs with a connection reset.
hints: Flaky tests erode trust in the whole suite.
Retries can hide real product bugs.
challenges.explanation:
Quarantining keeps the main signal trustworthy while the issue is investigated. Blind retries can hide a
       real BMC bug such as a web-server crash; deletion loses coverage.
challenges.source: Git, Jenkins & CI/CD Handbook · Ch. 16 Reliable Test Pipelines
options: Delete the test
Mark it as expected to fail permanently
Wrap the test in a loop that retries until it passes, forever
Quarantine it with a tracked issue, collect evidence from failures, and fix the root cause
